papers.title: LatentScore: An Open-Source Toolkit for Interactive Text-Steerable Procedural Audio
papers.abstract: LatentScore is an open-source Python toolkit for interactive multimedia systems that need text-steerable procedural audio, visual metadata, and live user control. Existing neural text-to-audio systems produce opaque waveforms. We instead treat prompt-to-audio as a control problem: a prompt such as morning coffee shop resolves to synthesizer parameters that the application can inspect and edit before rendering them as audio on CPU, and each generation also returns metadata—a title and a color palette—so downstream applications can keep sound and visuals in sync. The default backend resolves prompts against a prebuilt map of configurations—a single embedding lookup, in real time, with no GPU or API key. The map is curated offline from language-model-generated candidates, scored and selected automatically. The backend is swappable, so the same interface can instead route a prompt to a hosted LLM to generate the synthesizer parameters and associated metadata. The toolkit ships a Docker-packaged interactive demo, a Python SDK with streaming and live-steering APIs, and a CLI. LatentScore is built for games, XR, installations, creative coding, and research prototypes needing responsive, editable, reproducible audio. The code is publicly available under Apache 2.0 at https://github.com/prabal-rje/latentscore (includes a demo video), with a live demo at https://latentscore.com/demo, a Colab quickstart, and an immutable snapshot at a pinned commit.

Audio Flamingo Next: Next-Generation Open Audio-Language Models for Speech, Sound, and Music

Audio Flamingo Next (AF-Next) is the next-generation open large audio-language model in the Audio Flamingo series. `nvidia/audio-flamingo-next-hf` is the instruction-tuned checkpoint for general audio understanding, question answering, and conversation over speech, environmental sounds, and music. ## Description Compared with Audio Flamingo 3, AF-Next adds: - a stronger foundational audio-language model for speech, sound, and music - training data scaled beyond academic benchmarks using public and internet-scale sources - native long-audio support up to 30 minutes - stronger multilingual ASR, multi-talker speech understanding, and long-form captioning - timestamp-aware modeling through Rotary Time Embeddings (RoTE) This checkpoint corresponds to **AF-Next-Instruct**, the post-trained assistant variant. It is the best default checkpoint if you want: - general audio QA - instruction following - multi-turn audio chat - long-form audio understanding - timestamp-aware prompts ## Best For - standard audio QA and instruction following across speech, sound, and music - assistant-style responses for long-audio questions, follow-up questions, and multi-turn chat - speech understanding tasks such as ASR, paralinguistic understanding, and multilingual AST / speech translation - music captioning and broad audio description when you want a direct answer instead of a dense long-form caption ## AF-Next Variants | Checkpoint | Use when you need | | --- | --- | | `nvidia/audio-flamingo-next-hf` | default QA, chat, ASR / AST, and direct assistant-style answers | | `nvidia/audio-flamingo-next-think-hf` | explicit multi-step reasoning, timestamp-grounded evidence, and longer reasoning traces | | `nvidia/audio-flamingo-next-captioner-hf` | dense long-form captions, timestamped scene breakdowns, and more descriptive outputs | These Hub weights are released as an `audio-text-to-text` model. The broader AF-Next project also discusses streaming TTS and voice-to-voice interaction, but those components are not part of this checkpoint. **This model is for non-commercial research purposes only.** ## Usage ### Install AF-Next is supported in Transformers: ```bash pip install --upgrade pip pip install --upgrade transformers accelerate ``` ### Notes - The processor expects mono `16 kHz` audio. - Audio is internally processed in `30`-second windows. - The released processor is configured for up to `1800` seconds of audio, i.e. `30` minutes. - Prompting matters: this checkpoint is strongest when the task and output format are explicit. Ask directly for QA, ASR, AST, timestamps, or speaker labels instead of using a generic prompt. ### Prompt Guide | Task | Prompt | Recommended Checkpoint(s) | | --- | --- | --- | | ASR | `Transcribe the input speech.` | `Instruct`, `Think` | | AST | `Translate any speech you hear from into .` | `Instruct`, `Think` | | Short Audio Captioning | `Generate a caption for the input audio.` | `Captioner`, `Think` | | Long Audio Captioning | `Generate a detailed caption for the input audio. In the caption, transcribe all spoken content by all speakers in the audio precisely.` | `Captioner`, `Think` | | Music Captioning | `Summarize the track with precision: mention its musical style, BPM, key, arrangement, production choices, and the emotions or story it conveys.` | `Captioner`, `Instruct`, `Think` | | Lyrics | `Generate a lyrics transcription from the input song.` | `Instruct`, `Captioner`, `Think` | | QA | `What precise description did the commentator use for the punch that ended the fight?` | `Instruct`, `Think` | | Timestamped Multi-Talker ASR | `Transcribe the input audio. If multiple speakers are present, provide diarized transcripts with speaker labels.`
`[Speaker 1] ...`
`[Speaker 2] ...` | `Instruct`, `Think` | ### Single-Turn Audio + Text ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor model_id = "nvidia/audio-flamingo-next-hf" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModel.from_pretrained( model_id, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto", ).eval() conversation = [ [ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": ( "Transcribe the speech, identify important background sounds, " "and mention approximate timestamps for key events." ), }, { "type": "audio", "path": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/AudioSkills/resolve/main/assets/videoplayback_superman.wav", }, ], } ] ] batch = processor.apply_chat_template( conversation, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, return_dict=True, ).to(model.device) if "input_features" in batch: batch["input_features"] = batch["input_features"].to(model.dtype) generated = model.generate( **batch, max_new_tokens=1024, repetition_penalty=1.2, ) prompt_len = batch["input_ids"].shape[1] completion = generated[:, prompt_len:] text = processor.batch_decode( completion, skip_special_tokens=True, clean_up_tokenization_spaces=False, )[0] print(text) ``` ### Multi-Turn Follow-Up ```python conversation = [ [ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": ( "Transcribe the input speech, then keep the conversation open " "for follow-up questions." ), }, { "type": "audio", "path": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/AudioSkills/resolve/main/assets/WhDJDIviAOg_120_10.mp3", }, ], }, { "role": "assistant", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Summer follows spring, the days grow longer, and the nights are warm.", } ], }, { "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Summarize the content in one sentence.", } ], }, ] ] ``` ## Training Summary AF-Next is trained with a four-stage curriculum spanning pre-training, mid-training, post-training, and temporally grounded reasoning training. The paper describes: - AF-Whisper-based audio modeling with broader multilingual and multi-talker speech coverage - expanded training data from AudioSkills-XL, LongAudio-XL, AF-Think, AF-Chat, and MF-Skills - `45K` additional multi-talker speech samples - `200K+` long-form internet videos spanning roughly `5` to `30` minutes - `2M+` real-world short audio skill samples mined from long-form audio - `1M` multi-audio instruction examples - `30K` multi-turn chat examples - `386K` safety and instruction-following examples - multilingual ASR and AST data from Emilia, CoVoST, MUST, Amazon-SIFT, ALI Meeting, aidatatang, AISHELL, and Granary - training on `128` NVIDIA H100 GPUs AF-Next-Instruct is obtained after GRPO-based post-training focused on multi-turn chat, safety, instruction following, and selected AudioSkills-XL skills. ## Architecture The released checkpoint exposes `AudioFlamingoNextForConditionalGeneration` with `AudioFlamingoNextProcessor`. At a high level, AF-Next combines: - an AF-Whisper audio encoder using `128`-bin log-mel features - non-overlapping `30`-second audio chunking - a `2`-layer MLP audio adaptor - a Qwen2.5-family text backbone extended to long context - RoTE for timestamp-aware temporal grounding The released config uses: - `audio_config.hidden_size = 1280` - `audio_config.num_hidden_layers = 32` - `text_config.hidden_size = 3584` - `text_config.num_hidden_layers = 28` - `text_config.max_position_embeddings = 131072` ## Limitations The paper highlights several limitations: - internet-scale audio is still noisy and uneven across domains, languages, and acoustic conditions - low-resource languages, rare sound events, and specialized domains remain underrepresented - long-context reasoning is still difficult when relevant evidence is sparse or far apart in time - evaluation does not yet fully cover all supported capabilities, including multi-talker ASR, diarization, timestamped captioning, and voice-to-voice interaction For most users, this is the best AF-Next checkpoint to start with. If you need explicit long-form reasoning traces, use `nvidia/audio-flamingo-next-think-hf`. If you want the most verbose descriptive captions, use `nvidia/audio-flamingo-next-captioner-hf`. ## License / Terms of Use The model is released under the [NVIDIA OneWay Noncommercial License](static/NVIDIA-OneWay-Noncommercial-License_22Mar2022-academic.docx). Portions of the dataset generation are also subject to the [Qwen Research License](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B/blob/main/LICENSE) and OpenAI's [Terms of Use](https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{ghosh2026audioflamingonext, title={Audio Flamingo Next: Next-Generation Open Audio-Language Models for Speech, Sound, and Music}, author={Sreyan Ghosh and Arushi Goel and Kaousheik Jayakumar and Lasha Koroshinadze and Nishit Anand and Zhifeng Kong and Siddharth Gururani and Sang-gil Lee and Jaehyeon Kim and Aya Aljafari and Chao-Han Huck Yang and Sungwon Kim and Ramani Duraiswami and Dinesh Manocha and Mohammad Shoeybi and Bryan Catanzaro and Ming-Yu Liu and Wei Ping}, year={2026}, howpublished={Technical report}, url={https://afnext-umd-nvidia.github.io/} } ```

# 👑 JJ coders Suna AI v1.0 — Official Halloween 2026 Flagship Foundation Model

**JJ coders Suna AI v1.0** is an open-source **48 kHz stereo vocal and instrumental music generation system** engineered by **JJ Coders Group (Johan Jomet)**. It combines a **5-Billion Parameter Continuous Flow-Matching Diffusion Transformer (`ACE-Step 1.5 XL SFT`)**, **`Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`** lyric/phonetic conditioning, **14 Per-Genre Rank-64 DiT LoRA Experts**, a **15.8M-Parameter 12-Block Dilated ResNet-SE Masterpiece Critic (`SunaV1TitanMasterpieceNet`)**, and **48 kHz Stereo Melodic Soul Guides**.

* 🌐 **Official Website:** [suna.jjcoders.com](https://suna.jjcoders.com)
* 🎛️ **Live A100 Gradio Studio:** [huggingface.co/spaces/johanjomet/suna-ai-studio](https://huggingface.co/spaces/johanjomet/suna-ai-studio)
* 📦 **Model Hub Repository:** [huggingface.co/jjcoders/suna-v1](https://huggingface.co/jjcoders/suna-v1)

---

## 🚀 Key Architectural Breakthroughs in `Suna AI v1.0`

| Architectural Layer | Legacy Raw Open-Source Diffusion | JJ coders Suna AI v1.0 Flagship |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Vocal Pitch & Melody (`210–4,200 Hz`)** | Flat 1-note monotone "reading text aloud" | **Legato Melodic Soul Guide + `+12st` Octave Chorus Belt (`1.8 Oct` F0 range)** |
| **Intro Rhythm Lock (`0:00–0:15`)** | 20–35s of beatless silence or random noise | **Locked-in `0:00` Sub-Bass & Drum Pocket (`99.4%` groove lock)** |
| **Lyric & Phonetic Articulation** | 20s `"Oh-woah"` scream loops & shouted `[Drop]!` tags | **Syllable-Paced Phonetic Aligner + Multilingual G2P (`en`, `ml`, `fr`, `es`)** |
| **Candidate Selection** | Single blind random seed | **15.8M-Param `SunaV1TitanMasterpieceNet` (12 Dilated ResBlocks + SE)** |
| **Audio Fidelity & Mastering** | 16–32 kHz mono/muddy output | **True 48 kHz Stereo Oobleck VAE + `-14 LUFS` Mid-Side Mastering** |

---

## 📂 Repository Files & Multi-Format Checkpoints

* `model.safetensors` & `suna_v1_lora_experts.safetensors` — Official SafeTensors weights containing all 14 Rank-64 DiT LoRA Experts and the 15.8M-parameter `SunaV1TitanMasterpieceNet` Critic.
* `JJ_coders_Suna_AI_v1_Q4_K_M.gguf` & `JJ_coders_Suna_AI_v1_3_Q4_K_M.gguf` — Official binary GGUF v3 packages for local/edge runtimes.
* `suna_v1_ultimate_adapter.pt`, `suna_v1_halloween_10b_titan_adapter.pt`, & `suna_v2_1_pop_masterpiece_adapter.pt` — Unified PyTorch checkpoints for Colab & ZeroGPU Spaces.
* `suna_v1_dna_bank.json` & `config.json` — Melodic Soul harmonic profiles, BPM/key matrices, and model configuration.

# MuLaCover — Cover Song & Music Remix Generation

> 🎵 **Try HeartMuLa online — no GPU or setup needed:** [heartmula.com](https://heartmula.com)
> Make songs from lyrics, create covers and remixes, and edit any passage of a song in MuLa Studio. Free daily credits.

MuLaCover is a controllable AI cover-song and music-remix model. It transforms
reference music using lyrics and a structured text style prompt, or generates
from melody/chord MIDI. The standalone inference code is maintained in the
[MuLaCover repository](https://github.com/HeartMuLa/MuLaCover).

[HeartMuLa repository](https://github.com/HeartMuLa/heartlib) ·
[HeartMuLa paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10547) ·
[Try it online](https://heartmula.com)

> Model weights are publicly available for download. No access request is required.

## Inputs

Lyrics use section markers and preserved line breaks:

```text
[Verse]
One lyric line
Another lyric line

[Chorus]
One chorus line
```

Style is one UTF-8 line using named fields:

```text
topic:[Longing]; genre:[country]; instrument:[Strings,acoustic guitar]; mood:[hopeful]
```

## Download

Download the model weights with the Hugging Face CLI. Authentication is not required:

```bash
hf download HeartMuLa/MuLaCover --local-dir ./ckpt/MuLaCover
```

Also download HeartCodec and Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
into sibling checkpoint directories. Reference-audio conditioning also needs
the documented YourMT3 and ChordNet checkpoints. See the code repository for
the complete installation and generation commands.

## Usage

Install the `mulacover` package and prepare all checkpoint directories using
the [generation guide](https://github.com/HeartMuLa/MuLaCover/blob/main/examples/cover_song_generation.md).
Run the following from the code repository root. `./ckpt` is the parent
directory containing MuLaCover, HeartCodec, Qwen3, and the transcription models.

```python
import torch
from mulacover import MuLaCoverGenPipeline

torch.manual_seed(42)
pipe = MuLaCoverGenPipeline.from_pretrained(
    "./ckpt",
    device=torch.device("cuda:0"),
    dtype={
        "mulacover": torch.bfloat16,
        "codec": torch.float32,
        "qwen": torch.float32,
        "transcriptor": torch.float32,
    },
    lazy_load=True,
)
pipe(
    {
        "ref_audio": "/path/to/reference.mp3",
        "lyrics": "assets/lyrics.txt",
        "tags": "assets/tags.txt",
    },
    save_path="cover.wav",
)
```

The pipeline writes a WAV file. Use the MuLaCover package API shown above;
this model is not a built-in Transformers model class.

## Files

- `config.json`: MuLaCover model architecture configuration.
- `gen_config.json`: audio/text token identifiers used during generation.
- `model-00001-of-00005.safetensors` … `model-00005-of-00005.safetensors`:
  sharded model weights.
- `model.safetensors.index.json`: shard index.
- `tokenizer.json`: lyrics and prompt tokenizer.
- `SHA256SUMS`: release integrity checksums.

## License and use restrictions

The official model weights are licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0 with the additional
terms in `MODEL_LICENSE`. Commercial use of the official weights is prohibited
without separate written authorization from MuLa Labs.

Outputs generated using the official weights are restricted to noncommercial
use unless separately authorized in writing by MuLa Labs. The Apache-2.0
license covering the source-code repository does not grant commercial rights
to these weights or their generated outputs.

Users are responsible for obtaining the rights required for their lyrics,
reference audio, performances, voices, and generated works. Do not use the
model to impersonate a person deceptively or violate copyright, privacy, or
publicity rights.

## Community

Join the [MuLaCover Discord](https://discord.gg/Nf7SRkmWAE) for discussion and
community support. Reproducible software defects should be reported through
the code repository's GitHub Issues.

## Join MuLa Labs, Vera Praxis Lab

We are always excited to meet people with a strong interest in audio and music.
MuLa Labs has internship openings for candidates who want to build the next
generation of music and audio technology. To apply, email your resume or CV,
together with a short introduction, to
[contact@mulalabs.ai](mailto:contact@mulalabs.ai).

--- library_name: nemo license: other license_name: openmdw-1.1 license_link: https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/ pipeline_tag: automatic-speech-recognition language: - cs - nl - en - fr - de - hi - it - ko - pl - pt - ru - sk - es - bg - hr - da - et - fi - hu - ja - lv - lt - ro - sl - sv - th - tr - uk - ar - bn - zh - el - he - id - mt - mr - tl - ta - te - vi tags: - nvidia - pytorch - nemotron-3.5 - speech - asr - speech-translation - speaker-diarization - audio - transcription - speech-to-text - multilingual - timestamps - long-form-audio - language-identification - code-switching - audio-question-answering - instruction-following - hf-asr-leaderboard - transformers datasets: - nvidia/Granary-v2 base_model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B track_downloads: true --- # Sharded BF16 checkpoint This repository repackages [nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B) from revision `c17667641642c4265ff2b7037dd101b7d4567634` into **17 valid safetensors shards** (each smaller than 5 GB), for downloading over HTTPS with file-size limits. Tensor names, shapes, dtypes, and weight bytes are unchanged; no quantization was applied. Original safetensors metadata is preserved, with `format: pt` added. `model.safetensors.index.json` maps all 1395 tensors to their shards. Keep all shards and the index together. The original `config.json`, `llm_backbone/config.json`, tokenizer, processor, timestamp metadata and third-party license files are preserved. Architecture settings require no changes for standard safetensors sharding. No 67.5 GB monolithic file is included. Use `KirillFPV/nemotron-transcribe-parts` in place of the original repository ID with a compatible loader that supports sharded safetensors. For the Transformers integration, follow NVIDIA's installation requirements in the original model card below: ```python from transformers import AutoModelForMultimodalLM, AutoProcessor model_id = "KirillFPV/nemotron-transcribe-parts" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, device_map="auto") ``` For the Hugging Face CLI, disable the Xet client if necessary: ```bash HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 hf download KirillFPV/nemotron-transcribe-parts --local-dir ./nemotron-transcribe ``` Direct HTTPS downloads use `https://huggingface.co/KirillFPV/nemotron-transcribe-parts/resolve/main/` and must follow redirects. Disabling the Xet client does not bypass network restrictions on the serving domains. Verify downloaded files with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS`. See `sharding_manifest.json` for source and shard SHA256 checksums. The repacking process verified the source checksum, copied tensor bytes without decoding, verified each shard's copied data, and checked all shard headers using the native safetensors parser. GPU inference was not run as part of repacking. Upstream examples and benchmark claims below refer to the original NVIDIA release. --- # NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B
![Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe overview: one speech LLM transcribes a recording in the style selected by the instruction](hero.png) **Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight, offline speech and audio model** for transcription in 40 languages, with support for recordings up to one hour and a 65,536-token context. Its hybrid mixture-of-experts architecture activates approximately **4.3B parameters**, including the audio encoder, and it is released in [BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B), [FP8](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-FP8), and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4) precision. [Get started ↓](#quick-start) · [Explore the tasks ↓](#prompt-guide) · [See the evidence ↓](#results-at-a-glance) · [NeMo Speech ↗](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech)
Table of contents - [Model Summary](#model-summary) - [Results at a Glance](#results-at-a-glance) - [Efficiency](#efficiency) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Prompt Guide](#prompt-guide) - [Model Architecture](#model-architecture) - [Language Support Matrix](#language-support-matrix) - [Training, Testing, and Evaluation Datasets](#training-testing-and-evaluation-datasets) - [Benchmark Results](#benchmark-results) - [Inference Setup and Prompts](#inference-setup-and-prompts) - [Ethical Considerations](#ethical-considerations)

# Model Overview ### Description NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe is an offline speech and audio model that processes recordings, together with text instructions and optional context, into text responses. NVIDIA developed this [Speech-Augmented Language Model (SALM)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09424) for multilingual transcription, speech translation, contextual transcription, speaker-attributed transcription, rich transcription, timestamp prediction, language identification, and audio question answering. The training mixture also includes a small amount of text instruction following and PII tagging/redaction tasks. This model is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. ### Model Summary | | | |:---|:---| | **Total Parameters** | 34B (4.3B active), including the audio encoder | | **Architecture** | Mamba-2–Transformer hybrid Mixture of Experts language model with a Parallel Expert Encoder (Transformer ASR encoder and speaker encoder) | | **Precision** | BF16 (full-precision reference weights); [FP8](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-FP8) and [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-NVFP4) variants are available | | **Context Length** | 65,536 tokens; recordings up to 1 hour | | **Inputs / Outputs** | Audio and text / text, with optional word timestamps | | **Languages** | 40; see the [language support matrix](#language-support-matrix) | | **Tasks** | Transcription in verbatim or written form, contextual transcription, speaker-attributed transcription, rich transcription, speech translation, language identification, and audio question answering | | **Deployment** | 1× H100 80 GB; see the [hardware compatibility table](#software-integration) | | **Speculative Decoding** | Native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP); optional DFlash2 draft model | | **Reasoning Mode** | Configurable through the chat template (`enable_thinking=True/False`) | | **Recommended Sampling** | Transcription, translation, and language identification: temperature 0, reasoning off; audio understanding: temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, reasoning on | | **Best For** | Highest accuracy, customization, and fine-tuning | | **License** | [OpenMDW-1.1](https://openmdw.ai/license/1-1/) | ### Results at a Glance Results captured on October 12, 2026. Error rates are percentages. **↓ Lower is better.** Complete results are listed under [Benchmark Results](#benchmark-results). **Best published results** | Capability | Benchmark | Metric | Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe | Next best published | |:---|:---|:---|:---|:---| | Multi-speaker ASR | AMI, CALLHOME, Mixer 6, NOTSOFAR-1 full sessions | Mean cpWER ↓ | **15.80** | DiCoW v3.3 + DiariZen 16.83 | | Style control | Preference-ASR | WER ↓, default / instructed | **7.56 / 6.16** | Canary-Qwen 8.16 / 8.36 | **Best open-weight results** | Capability | Benchmark | Metric | Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe | Next best open-weight model | |:---|:---|:---|:---|:---| | English ASR | Open ASR Leaderboard, 9 public sets | Mean WER ↓ | **4.71** | Qwen3-ASR-1.7B 4.94 | | Long-form ASR | Open ASR Leaderboard, long-form | Mean WER ↓ | **10.98** | Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v3 13.37 | | Multilingual ASR | Multilingual Open ASR Leaderboard, 7 languages | Mean WER ↓ | **4.62** | Qwen3-ASR-1.7B 6.49 | ### Efficiency ![Throughput versus median request latency of the Nemotron Transcribe NIM on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU for BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 with and without speculative decoding](serving_performance.png) With the optimized vLLM implementation in the Nemotron Transcribe NIM, one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPU transcribes up to 2,238 seconds of audio per second (NVFP4 with DFlash2 speculative decoding) and returns the transcript of a 30-second recording in 0.13 seconds. Install both into one environment with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and download the checkpoint: ```bash git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech.git nemo-speech cd nemo-speech uv venv --python 3.13 .venv UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=$PWD/.venv uv sync --extra asr --extra vllm --locked --no-install-project uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps -e . # PyAV decodes compressed audio formats, such as M4A, without a system FFmpeg. uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps av==19.0.2 # vLLM requires OpenCV, which NeMo's dependency settings exclude. uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps opencv-python-headless==5.0.0.93 source .venv/bin/activate hf download nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B --local-dir ./NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B ``` #### Start the Server Start an OpenAI-compatible server on one GPU, with MTP speculative decoding proposing eight tokens (MTP8): ```bash export VLLM_PLUGINS=nemo_speechlm # Allow vLLM to decode recordings up to one hour long (the default is 600 seconds). export VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S=3600 export VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB=180 # Word timestamps require the V1 model runner. export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 vllm serve ./NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B \ --served-model-name nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B \ --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 \ --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 192 \ --enable-chunked-prefill --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --use-replayssm --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-cache-mode none \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --no-async-scheduling \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"audio":{"count":6,"length":120000000}}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":8}' \ --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 \ --trust-request-mm-kwargs \ --middleware nemo.collections.speechlm2.vllm.salm.ctc_serving.ctc_timestamp_middleware ``` The server listens on `127.0.0.1:8000`; use `--host` and `--port` to change this. The settings target an H100 with 80 GB of GPU memory; other hardware or workloads may need a different `--gpu-memory-utilization`, `--max-model-len`, or `--max-num-seqs`. The `--middleware` and `--trust-request-mm-kwargs` options let requests opt into [word timestamps](#word-timestamps-and-speaker-diarization). To change the configuration, modify the command as follows: | Configuration | Change | | --- | --- | | Eight GPUs: one data-parallel engine per GPU, with expert parallelism (TP=1, DP=8, EP=8) | Add `--data-parallel-size 8 --api-server-count 8 --enable-expert-parallel --disable-custom-all-reduce` | | MTP with two proposed tokens (MTP2) | Set `"num_speculative_tokens":2` | | No speculative decoding | Remove `--speculative-config` | #### Speculative Decoding Speculative decoding proposes several tokens at once and verifies them with the main model. The checkpoint contains two MTP depths implemented with a repeated layer. MTP8 reuses that layer to propose eight tokens; it does not require eight distinct trained MTP layers. The best mode depends on the GPU and the workload. Approximate throughput for batched English ASR on **one NVIDIA H100 80 GB**, using tuned serving settings: | Decoding mode | Approximate BF16 RTFx | | --- | ---: | | MTP off | Not measured | | MTP2 | 410 | | MTP8 | 270 | | DFlash2 K=7 | 340 | | DFlash2 K=15 | 260 | RTFx is total audio duration divided by processing time: 340 RTFx means about 340 seconds of audio processed per second under batch load. These are rough throughput estimates, excluding server startup, for the English Open ASR and Monsoon datasets with reasoning disabled. Throughput depends on recording length, output length, batch size, and GPU memory settings; it is not a single-request latency estimate. Keep ReplaySSM (`--use-replayssm --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-cache-mode none`) and prefix caching disabled, as in the command above. The first requests after startup are slower while kernels are compiled and warmed up.
DFlash2 draft model As an alternative to MTP, the separate draft model [`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-DFlash2) proposes up to 15 tokens at once with vLLM's `dflash` method. DFlash2 and MTP are alternatives and are not combined. K=7 is the recommended starting point; K=15 was slower on the tested ASR workload. vLLM 0.32.0 needs a small fix to its DFlash2 implementation; without it, the server can fail when requests finish. Apply it once to the environment: ```bash python - <<'EOF_PATCH' from pathlib import Path import vllm path = Path(vllm.__file__).parent / "model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash2.py" source = path.read_text() if "safe_anchor_token_ids" not in source: old = " successors = successor_table[candidate_ids]\n" anchor = " anchor_token_ids[:, None, None].expand(-1, 1, top_k)," assert source.count(old) == 1 and source.count(anchor) == 1, "unexpected vLLM version" source = source.replace(old, ( " safe_anchor_token_ids = anchor_token_ids.clamp(\n" " min=0, max=predecessor_table.shape[0] - 1\n" " )\n" + old )).replace(anchor, " safe_anchor_token_ids[:, None, None].expand(-1, 1, top_k),") path.write_text(source) EOF_PATCH ``` The fix modifies vLLM source code (Copyright contributors to the vLLM project), which is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, not under OpenMDW-1.1; see [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Word timestamps are not available with DFlash2, so the CTC alignment is disabled: ```bash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7,"model":"nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B-DFlash2"}' \ --hf-overrides '{"ctc_timestamps":{"enabled":false}}' ``` vLLM runs DFlash2 only on its V2 model runner, so also run `unset VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` before starting the server.
#### Send a Request Send audio to the `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with an OpenAI-compatible client. The following function covers transcription, reasoning, and word timestamps: ```python import base64 from pathlib import Path from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY") def ask(audio_path, prompt, system_prompt="", reasoning=False, timestamps=False): audio = base64.b64encode(Path(audio_path).read_bytes()).decode() messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt}] if system_prompt else [] messages.append({"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": prompt}, {"type": "audio_url", "audio_url": {"url": f"data:audio/wav;base64,{audio}"}}, ]}) extra_body = { "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": reasoning}, "skip_special_tokens": False, # keep speaker and event tags "spaces_between_special_tokens": False, "seed": 0, } if reasoning: extra_body.update(top_k=-1, thinking_token_budget=17408) extra_body["chat_template_kwargs"]["reasoning_budget"] = 16384 if timestamps: extra_body["mm_processor_kwargs"] = {"capture_ctc_timestamps": True} return client.chat.completions.create( model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B", messages=messages, temperature=0.6 if reasoning else 0, top_p=0.95 if reasoning else 1.0, max_tokens=20480 if reasoning else 16384, extra_body=extra_body, ) response = ask("audio.wav", "Transcribe the following audio.") print(response.choices[0].message.content) ``` A dense one-hour conversation can need about 20,000 output tokens. For long recordings, raise `max_tokens` or remove it, so that the transcript is not truncated. Transcription uses temperature 0 with reasoning disabled. For audio understanding, enable reasoning and ask a question about the audio: ```python response = ask("audio.wav", "What is happening in this audio?", reasoning=True) ``` This sets temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k disabled, seed 0, a 20,480-token completion limit, and a 16,384-token reasoning budget with a 1,024-token allowance to finish reasoning. Use the task instructions documented under [Evaluation Prompts](#evaluation-prompts) as `prompt` and `system_prompt`. #### Word Timestamps and Speaker Diarization The checkpoint bundles the CTC heads used to align the generated transcript to the audio. With `--middleware` set as in the server command above, request timestamps with `timestamps=True`, together with a speaker-tagged transcription prompt: ```python response = ask("audio.wav", ( "Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. " "Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. " "Write numbers in their standard written form. " "Put speaker tags on the transcription." ), timestamps=True) alignment = response.model_dump()["ctc_timestamps"] if alignment["error"] is not None: raise RuntimeError(alignment["error"]) for word in alignment["words"]: print(word["word"], word["start"], word["end"], word["speaker"]) ``` The response contains a top-level `ctc_timestamps` object: - `words`: word text, start and end times in seconds relative to the input audio, and the transcript's speaker tag. - `diarization`: speaker activity segments derived from the audio. - `speaker_tag_to_diarization_speaker`: the mapping between transcript tags and diarization speakers. - `error`: `null` on success, or an alignment failure reason. Check this field before using the timestamps. Timestamp requests accept one audio recording, `stream=false`, and `n=1`. Keep `skip_special_tokens=false` and ask for speaker tags when speaker attribution is needed. A transcript without speaker tags is aligned as a single speaker. Use the `diarization` segments, rather than word timestamps, when evaluating diarization. ### SGLang-Omni [SGLang-Omni](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni) serves this model for whole-file transcription on `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, on one GPU, from the BF16 or FP8 checkpoint (both validated on one H100 80 GB and one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell). It does not need NeMo. After [installing SGLang-Omni](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/docs/get_started/installation.md) 0.2.0, which pins SGLang 0.5.22: ```bash sgl-omni serve \ --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B \ --model-name nemotron-transcribe \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --port 8000 curl http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions \ -F model=nemotron-transcribe \ -F file=@audio.wav ``` Word timestamps, speaker-attributed output, translation and speculative decoding are not part of this integration. See the [SGLang-Omni Nemotron Transcribe cookbook](https://sgl-project.github.io/sglang-omni/cookbook/nemotron_transcribe.html) for its settings, streaming and a tuned profile for short clips. ### Transformers usage 🤗 Install 🤗 Transformers from source: ```sh pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers ```
Transcription ```python from transformers import AutoModelForMultimodalLM, AutoProcessor model_id = "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B" samples = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/dummy-audio-samples/resolve/main/" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, device_map="auto") audio = [samples + "en-Alice_woman.wav", samples + "diarization_example.mp3"] speaker_attributed_prompt = ( "Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write " "numbers in their standard written form. Put speaker tags on the transcription." ) prompt = [None, speaker_attributed_prompt] inputs = processor.apply_transcription_request(audio, prompt=prompt).to(model.device) outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024) texts = processor.decode(outputs[:, inputs.input_ids.shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=False) print([text.replace(processor.tokenizer.pad_token, "") for text in texts]) ```
Speaker-attributed transcription ```python from transformers import AutoModelForMultimodalLM, AutoProcessor model_id = "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B" samples = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/dummy-audio-samples/resolve/main/" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, device_map="auto") prompt = ( "Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write " "numbers in their standard written form. Put speaker tags on the transcription." ) conversation = [ { "role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": prompt}, {"type": "audio", "path": samples + "diarization_example.mp3"}, ], } ] inputs = processor.apply_chat_template( conversation, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, return_dict=True, enable_thinking=False, ).to(model.device) outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024) text = processor.decode(outputs[0, inputs.input_ids.shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=False) print(text) ``` `processor.extract_speaker_dict` splits the output into one dictionary per speaker turn: ```python for turn in processor.extract_speaker_dict(text): print(turn) ```
Word timestamps and speaker diarization Requires `torchaudio` and `scipy`. ```python from transformers import AutoModelForMultimodalLM, AutoProcessor model_id = "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B" samples = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/hf-internal-testing/dummy-audio-samples/resolve/main/" processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, device_map="auto") prompt = ( "Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write " "numbers in their standard written form. Put speaker tags on the transcription." ) inputs = processor.apply_transcription_request(samples + "diarization_example.mp3", prompt=prompt).to(model.device) outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, return_word_timestamp_logits=True) texts = processor.decode(outputs.sequences[:, inputs.input_ids.shape[1] :], skip_special_tokens=False) timestamps = processor.align_word_timestamps( texts, outputs.word_timestamp_logits, inputs.input_features_mask, outputs.speaker_logits, ) print(timestamps[0]["chunks"][:3]) ```
See the [Transformers documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/nemotron3_5_transcribe) for more. ### Evaluation Prompts Use these shortened task-specific templates as starting points. For ASR evaluation, use [Exact ASR Benchmark Prompts](#exact-asr-benchmark-prompts). The ASR benchmark environment uses vLLM 0.28.0 and NeMo Speech with the FP32 preservation change from [PR #16357](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Speech/pull/16357), which is included in the main branch, with MTP2. For audio understanding, spoken instructions, and text reasoning, use [Exact Understanding and Reasoning Prompts](#exact-understanding-and-reasoning-prompts), which lists the complete evaluated system prompts; keep the prepared user questions and choices unchanged. For the remaining benchmark families, use [All Evaluated Prompts](#all-evaluated-prompts), which contains the complete evaluated prompts and reasoning flags. Replace placeholders with the actual languages, labels, or context. #### Prompt Recommendations For these tasks, keep the **system prompt empty**. Send the instruction in the **user message**, alongside the audio. | Task | Recommended user prompt | Why we suggest it | | --- | --- | --- | | Verbatim ASR, including multilingual and long-form audio | `Audio transcription. Language: as spoken. Wording: verbatim, including fillers and repetitions. Formatting: punctuation and capitalization. Output: transcript only.` | Preserves wording and language with an explicit output format. | | Clean written transcript | Replace the wording clause above with `omit fillers and accidental repetitions; keep the remaining spoken wording unchanged`. Add `numbers in their standard written form` if needed. | Makes cleanup and number normalization explicit. | | Speaker attribution / word timestamps | `Transcribe this audio with punctuation and capitalization. Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write numbers in their standard written form. Put speaker tags on the transcription.` | Provides stable speaker tags for attribution and timestamp alignment; also enable timestamp capture. | | Near-field speaker only (experimental) | `Transcribe this audio. Include all spoken words and verbal fillers. Write numbers as spoken. No punctuation or capitalization. Transcribe only the speaker nearest to the microphone. Do not transcribe any other voices.` | Ignores background voices, such as far-field speech in a meeting room. With LibriSpeech test-clean speech mixed with far-field NOTSOFAR-1 audio, the WER is 4.78% with this prompt and 27.32% with a single-speaker transcription prompt. | | Code-switching / script control | `Transcribe verbatim in the original languages. # Stable Audio Open Small — Core AI (on-device music generation)

**The model zoo's first MUSIC / AUDIO generation model for Apple Core AI.** Type a prompt, get ~11s
of 44.1 kHz stereo audio — generated entirely **on-device** on Apple Silicon. A community port of
[`stabilityai/stable-audio-open-small`](https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-audio-open-small)
(Stability AI + Arm) to Core AI.

A latent **diffusion** text-to-audio model: a T5 text encoder conditions a DiT (diffusion transformer)
that denoises a latent over **8 rectified-flow steps**, then an Oobleck VAE decodes the latent to a
waveform. Distilled (ARC) for few-step generation, so it's fast.

<!-- gen-cards:use-it begin id=stable-audio-open-small (managed by scripts/gen-cards — edit cards.json / QuickStart.swift, not this block) -->
![Stable Audio Open Small demo](https://huggingface.co/mlboydaisuke/Stable-Audio-Open-Small-CoreAI/resolve/main/demo.gif)
*Stable Audio Open Small on iPhone 17 Pro — the zoo's coreai-audio app, 12 s of audio in ~1 s.*

## Use it

**New to Core AI? [Start with CoreAIKit 0.8.0](https://github.com/john-rocky/coreai-kit#readme).** Follow its requirements and first-run steps for `qwen3-0.6b`, then open the same release's [ChatDemo](https://github.com/john-rocky/coreai-kit/tree/0.8.0/Examples/ChatDemo). The README records the tested OS/SDK and download size; model and device coverage is stated per example.

⚡ **One line** — this model is the default behind the kit's task op
(`import CoreAIOps`; no session, no model plumbing, downloads on first use):

```swift
let audio = try await CoreAI.compose(prompt)
```

Every op, one shape — [Cookbook](https://github.com/john-rocky/coreai-kit/blob/0.8.0/docs/COOKBOOK.md).

▶️ **Run it (source)** — the [Music runner](https://github.com/john-rocky/coreai-kit/tree/0.8.0/Examples/Music)
(GUI + CLI, one app for every text-to-music model in the catalog):

```bash
git clone --branch 0.8.0 --depth 1 https://github.com/john-rocky/coreai-kit
export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-27.0.0-RC.app/Contents/Developer
open -a /Applications/Xcode-27.0.0-RC.app coreai-kit/Examples/Music/Music.xcodeproj
# → Run, then pick "Stable Audio Open Small" in the model picker

# agents / headless (macOS):
cd coreai-kit/Examples/Music
swift run -c release music-cli --model stable-audio-open-small --prompt "128 BPM tech house drum loop" --output loop.wav
```

Use Xcode build **27A266a** from the release's `.xcode-pin`; adjust the app path if your installation is named differently.

💻 **Build with it** — complete; the glue is kit API, copy-paste runs:

```swift
import CoreAIKit

let musician = try await KitMusician(catalog: "stable-audio-open-small")
let audio = try await musician.generate(prompt)
// audio.samples: 44.1 kHz stereo (planar L/R) — play it or write a WAV
```

The take-home is [`Examples/Music/Sources/QuickStart.swift`](https://github.com/john-rocky/coreai-kit/blob/0.8.0/Examples/Music/Sources/QuickStart.swift)
— this exact code as one typed function, no UI; the CLI is an argument shell over it, and
the GUI drives the same `KitMusician(catalog:)` and plays the result.
Length? `generate(_:seconds:)` up to the model's ~11 s window. The WAV container is your
app's territory (the runner ships a 30-line writer with planar-stereo support).

**Integration checklist**

- SPM: `https://github.com/john-rocky/coreai-kit` (exact **0.8.0**) → product **CoreAIKit**
- Info.plist: none needed
- Entitlements: none needed (macOS)
- First run downloads the model — ~1,060 MB (Mac) — then it loads from the
  local cache (Application Support; progress via the `downloadProgress` callback)
- Measure in Release — Debug is ~3× slower on per-token host work
<!-- gen-cards:use-it end -->

## What's in the bundle (`macos/`)

Three Core AI `.aimodel` bundles + a tiny host sampler loop:

| bundle | role | I/O |
|---|---|---|
| `sa_cond_fp16b` | T5-base encoder + number conditioner | `input_ids[1,64], attention_mask[1,64], seconds_norm[1] → cross_attn_cond[1,65,768], global_embed[1,768], cond_mask[1,65]` |
| `sa_dit_fp16` | diffusion transformer (run 8×) | `x[1,64,256], t[1], cross_attn_cond, global_embed, cross_attn_cond_mask → v[1,64,256]` |
| `sa_vae_fp16` | Oobleck VAE decoder | `latent[1,64,256] → audio[1,2,524288]` |

**Host loop** (`StableAudioRunner`): tokenize (T5, `t5_tokenizer/`) → conditioner → start from Gaussian
noise → 8-step rectified-flow euler `x = x + (t_next − t)·v` over the fixed schedule
`[1.0, .9944, .9845, .9579, .8909, .7455, .5125, .2739] → 0` → VAE decode → 44.1 kHz stereo wav.
No KV cache, no CFG (cfg_scale 1.0 — the model is ARC-distilled).

## Performance (M4 Max, GPU)

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| 8-step DiT | ~200 ms (25 ms/step) |
| VAE decode | ~185 ms |
| **total** | **~0.4 s for ~11.9 s of audio (~30× real-time)** |
| size | fp16, ~1.0 GB (DiT 651M + cond 210M + VAE 149M) |

Numerics: each bundle engine-gated vs the reference at cos ≥ 0.9999; full pipeline reproduces the
reference audio exactly.

# TTS accent ivoirien (Noushi et Franco-Bété) — V6 Qwen3-TTS + RVC v2 & V5 XTTS-v2

Modèle de synthèse vocale expressive (**Text-to-Speech / Clonage Vocal**) spécialisé dans le **français ivoirien naturel** (registre **Nouchi** et **Franco-Bété**).

- **Pipeline V6 recommandé (`qwen3_rvc_v6`)** : **Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base (Multi-Réf ICL)** pour la prosodie, le rythme et les tournures nouchi, suivi d'une passe **RVC v2 (Applio, 40 kHz)** entraînée **120 époques (2 400 steps)** par locuteur (`rmvpe` + `contentvec`).
- **Pipeline V5 hérité (`xtts_v5`)** : modèle **`coqui/XTTS-v2`** conservé à la racine du dépôt avec 3 locuteurs (`issouf`, `isaac`, `seitonne`) et 12 Special Tokens Atomiques d'émotions.

---

## Nouveautés V6 & Voix disponibles

1. **Architecture hybride V6 (Prosodie Qwen3 Multi-Réf + Timbre RVC v2 40 kHz)** :
   - **Étape 1 — Prosodie & accent (`Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base`)** : clonage vocal ICL (`x_vector_only_mode=False`, `language="French"`) conditionné par des références multi-clips nettoyées et transcrites mot à mot (`ref_multiref_<locuteur>.wav` / `.txt`).
   - **Étape 2 — Conversion spectrale (`RVC v2` Applio, 40 000 Hz)** : projection sur le modèle RVC v2 du locuteur cible (`f0_method="rmvpe"`, `embedder_model="contentvec"`, `index_rate=0.65`) pour un timbre chaud, net et naturel en **40 kHz**.
2. **2 voix V6 haute fidélité (`qwen3_rvc_v6/`)** :
   - `issouf` — timbre grave, posé et expressif (86 clips / 8.53 min d'entraînement RVC v2, `120 epochs`, `2 400 steps`).
   - `isaac` — timbre dynamique et spontané (87 clips / 8.17 min d'entraînement RVC v2, `120 epochs`, `2 400 steps`).
3. **3 voix V5 XTTS-v2 conservées (`references_voix/`)** : `issouf`, `isaac`, `seitonne`.

---

## Installation (Pipeline V6)

### 1. Dépendances Qwen3-TTS Multi-Réf (Python)

```bash
pip install -U "qwen-tts" "huggingface_hub>=0.27.0" "soundfile" "numpy>=2.0.0,<2.3.0"
pip install --no-deps torchaudio
```

### 2. Applio pour la passe RVC v2 (40 kHz)

Pour bénéficier du timbre final RVC v2 en 40 kHz, clonez [Applio](https://github.com/IAHispano/Applio) et indiquez son chemin via `--dossier-applio` (ou `dossier_applio="..."` en Python) :

```bash

cd Applio && pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Utilisation V6 (recommandée)

```bash
  --locuteur issouf \
  --dossier-applio /chemin/vers/Applio \
  --index-rate 0.65 \
  --texte "Dja, les môgôs ont dit que c'est gâté, mais nous on sait que ça va aller même." \
```

```bash

  --moteur qwen3_rvc_v6 \
```

# FireRedTTS3-Base — Russian adaptation

This is a full FP32 checkpoint with the supplied Russian LoRA merged into the
FireRedTTS3 Base core. No separate adapter is needed for serving. The package
includes the tokenizer, RedAE and CAM++ assets required for zero-shot cloning.

The packaging template is [CKermit/FireRedTTS3-Base](https://huggingface.co/CKermit/FireRedTTS3-Base)
at commit `53f8b59c3252f15d539a9205fbcab3e334a36b9f`. Its core/RedAE/CAM++ files were verified to be
identical to the original local base used by the adapter. The training base is
bound by its complete artifact fingerprint, recorded in `export_provenance.json`.

Merge validation checked PEFT layer outputs before/after merge, unchanged frozen
tensors, every saved core tensor, and the effective tokenizer. This is **not** an
end-to-end SGLang GPU parity test. Runtime precision and generation settings can
change the output compared with the training inference pipeline.

## SGLang Omni

Use SGLang **Omni** with FireRedTTS3 support. The inspected integration is
[PR #3005](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/3005), revision `718b51d52a2cffe2218f9c6a1ae076756eb8a505`; an older SGLang/Omni installation
does not provide this model. Follow its installation prerequisites in a separate
environment from training. Download the entire model repository.

From the compatible sglang-omni checkout, serve the downloaded directory:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 sgl-omni serve \
  --model-path /absolute/path/to/downloaded-model \
  --config examples/configs/firered_tts3_base.yaml \
  --allowed-local-media-path /absolute/path/to/reference-audio \
  --port 8000
```

Wait for `/health` to return HTTP 200. Call `/v1/audio/speech` with `language`
set to `Russian`, a target `input`, and one `references` entry containing
`audio_path` and the reference recording's actual `text`. Output is 24 kHz mono.
The inspected API limits `input` to 400 characters. See `UPSTREAM_MODEL_CARD.md`
and the integration cookbook for streaming and generation settings.

## Provenance and license

Original model: [FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3](https://huggingface.co/FireRedTeam/FireRedTTS3).
Packaging: CKermit / SGLang Omni. The original Apache-2.0 license is included in
`LICENSE`; upstream attribution and usage guidance are retained in
`UPSTREAM_MODEL_CARD.md`. This package contains modified model weights.
The LoRA profile is `backbone`. Training audio, reference recordings,
optimizer state and authentication credentials are not part of this release.

## Reported evaluation before merging

The supplied standalone-pipeline comparison contains 12 cases
and 4 speakers. Mean speaker-similarity delta:
`-0.00467739`; worst per-speaker mean delta:
`-0.01187599`; mean WER delta:
`0.00520833`. These are absolute metric differences against
the supplied baseline, not percentages of perceptual quality. A small benchmark
does not establish general voice-cloning or prosody parity. These scores were
not measured in SGLang or on the merged checkpoint. Report hashes and scorer IDs
are recorded in `export_provenance.json`; no reference audio/text is published.

# phoonnx-styletts2

Mirror of StyleTTS2-family checkpoints exported to ONNX for
[phoonnx](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx), OpenVoiceOS's offline TTS
library. StyleTTS2 generates speech conditioned on a style vector that
encodes prosody and timbre from a reference clip, which is what enables
zero-shot cloning; `phoonnx` also treats the Kokoro checkpoints (a StyleTTS2
descendant, "misaki"-phonemized) as `styletts2`-engine voices since they
share the same style-vector conditioning contract. See
[docs/cloning.md](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/cloning.md)
for the `styletts2_style` d-vector mechanism.

This repository holds the raw ONNX weights, `config.json` files, and (for
cloning-capable voices) `.bin` style vectors consumed by `phoonnx`'s
`voice_index` (`styletts2.json`); it is not meant to be browsed for voices
directly — use `phoonnx`'s voice manager, which resolves voice IDs to the
files here.

## Contents

| Directory | Voices | Language | Upstream |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ddatt-en-styletts2/` | `ddatt/en-styletts2` | en-US | community StyleTTS2 checkpoint by `ddatt`; original training source could not be located |
| `bsc-es-styletts2/` | `bsc/es-styletts2` (zero-shot) + 6 named speakers `bsc/es-cml<id>` | es | [`BSC-LT/styletts2-spanish-multispeaker`](https://huggingface.co/BSC-LT/styletts2-spanish-multispeaker) (Barcelona Supercomputing Center) |
| `bsc-ca-styletts2/` | `bsc/ca-styletts2` (zero-shot) + 11 named speakers `bsc/ca-<name>` | ca | [`BSC-LT/styletts2-catalan-multispeaker`](https://huggingface.co/BSC-LT/styletts2-catalan-multispeaker) (Barcelona Supercomputing Center) |
| `hitz-eu-styletts2/` | one speaker each: `antton`, `maider` | eu | [`HiTZ/StyleTTS2-eu`](https://huggingface.co/HiTZ/StyleTTS2-eu) (HiTZ Center, University of the Basque Country) |
| `hitz-eu-emo-styletts2/` | `antton`/`maider` x `happy`/`neutral`/`sad` | eu | [`HiTZ/StyleTTS2-eu_emo`](https://huggingface.co/HiTZ/StyleTTS2-eu_emo) (HiTZ Center) |
| `proxectonos-gl-celtia/` | `proxectonos/celtia-styletts2` | gl | [`proxectonos/Nos_StyleTTS2-Celtia-GL`](https://huggingface.co/proxectonos/Nos_StyleTTS2-Celtia-GL) ([Proxecto Nós](https://nos.gal/gl/proxecto-nos), technical development by [Gradiant](https://www.gradiant.org/)) |
| `proxectonos-gl-brais/` | `proxectonos/brais-styletts2` | gl | [`proxectonos/Nos_StyleTTS2-Brais-GL`](https://huggingface.co/proxectonos/Nos_StyleTTS2-Brais-GL) ([Proxecto Nós](https://nos.gal/gl/proxecto-nos), technical development by [Gradiant](https://www.gradiant.org/)) |
| `kokoro-82m/` | `kokoro/*` (English voices, plus per-language configs for es/fr/hi/it/ja/pt/zh) | en-US + others | [`hexgrad/Kokoro-82M`](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M); style vectors fetched at load time from [`onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX`](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX) |
| `kokoro-v0.19/` | Kokoro v0.19 voices | en-US | [`hexgrad/kLegacy`](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/kLegacy) (Kokoro v0.19) |
| `kokoro-v1.1-zh/` | Kokoro v1.1 zh/en voices | zh, en-US | [`hexgrad/Kokoro-82M-v1.1-zh`](https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M-v1.1-zh) |

## Usage

```python
import wave
from phoonnx.model_manager import TTSModelManager

manager = TTSModelManager()
manager.load()
manager.merge_default_voices()

voice = manager.voices["kokoro/af_heart"].load()
with wave.open("out.wav", "wb") as wav_file:
    voice.synthesize_wav("Hello, this is a test.", wav_file)
```

## License

`license: other` because the checkpoints in this repository come from
different labs with different licenses. `phoonnx` itself is Apache-2.0.

| Family | Voices | License |
|---|---|---|
| Kokoro (all versions) | `kokoro/*` | Apache-2.0 |
| BSC Spanish StyleTTS2 | `bsc/es-styletts2`, `bsc/es-cml*` | Apache-2.0 |
| BSC Catalan StyleTTS2 | `bsc/ca-styletts2`, `bsc/ca-*` | GPL-3.0 |
| ProxectoNós Galician StyleTTS2 | `proxectonos/celtia-styletts2`, `proxectonos/brais-styletts2` | Apache-2.0 |
| HiTZ Basque StyleTTS2 (base + emotion) | `hitz-eu-styletts2/*`, `hitz-eu-emo-styletts2/*` | Apache-2.0 |
| `ddatt/en-styletts2` | `ddatt-en-styletts2/` | not determined — original upstream repo could not be located; treat as all-rights-reserved until clarified |

The two BSC checkpoints are **multispeaker**. Neither upstream repository ships
reference audio, so `bsc/es-styletts2` and `bsc/ca-styletts2` need a reference
clip on every call. Alongside them each directory now carries one
`<speaker>.bin` style blob per named speaker, so the same checkpoint also
serves ordinary preset voices:

* `bsc-ca-styletts2/` — 11 [Festcat](https://huggingface.co/datasets/projecte-aina/festcat_trimmed_denoised)
  speakers: `bet eli eva jan mar ona pau pep pol teo uri`.
* `bsc-es-styletts2/` — the 6 [CML-TTS](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ylacombe/cml-tts)
  Spanish speakers that hold the corpus: `3946 8882 9972 10246 11797 12367`.
  CML-TTS names speakers by number only.

Each blob is 256 `float32` values (`ref_p` ++ `ref_s`), the mean of the style
encoder's output over four reference clips of that speaker taken from the
model's own training corpus. A named speaker still clones when you pass a
reference clip. See
[docs/bsc_multispeaker.md](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/bsc_multispeaker.md).

The Galician voices are single-speaker: each ships a `style.bin` default
style alongside the `style_encoder.onnx` used for cloning. They are
phonemized with Cotovía notation (not IPA) — see
[docs/galician.md](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/galician.md).

Note the BSC Catalan checkpoint is GPL-3.0-licensed by its authors; this only
governs the model weights themselves, not `phoonnx` (Apache-2.0), which
merely loads them.
